candidates.name: Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica
support_spans: Radiography showed complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption

candidates.why: The radiographic findings of bone resorption and the 'salt-and-pepper' appearance of the skull are characteristic of this condition, often associated with hyperparathyroidism.

candidates.name: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
support_spans: Histopathology of finger tumor
Numerous giant cells with multiple osteoclastlike nuclei and giant multinucleated cells dispersed in contact with fibers associated with small vessels
candidates.why: The presence of a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger with histopathological features of fibrous tissue, woven bone, and giant cells is consistent with a brown tumor, a rare complication of hyperparathyroidism.

candidates.name: Parathyroid carcinoma
support_spans: Elevated serum parathyroid hormone at 380 pmol/L
Sestamibi parathyroid scintigraphy identified hyperfunctional nodule
candidates.why: The extremely high level of parathyroid hormone and the presence of a hyperfunctional nodule on sestamibi scintigraphy raise the possibility of parathyroid carcinoma, a rare cause of primary hyperparathyroidism.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be challenging to consider due to its rarity and the fact that it can be mistaken for a parathyroid adenoma.
